problem: If the path $C$ is a part of the parabola $y={x}^{2}-1$ traversed from the point $A(0,-1)$ to point $B(2,3),$ then ${\int }_{C}5{x}^{2}y\,dx+{x}^{2}(y+1)\,dy=$
worked_solution:
Notice that our curve is given by the explicit Cartesian equation $y={x}^{2}-1.$ As a result, we obtain the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j=t\,i+({t}^{2}-1)\,j,\,t\in [0,2]\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=i+2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}5{x}^{2}y\,dx+{x}^{2}(y+1)\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{2}5{x}^{2}y\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+{x}^{2}(y+1)\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(5{x}^{2}y\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+{x}^{2}(y+1)\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}5{t}^{2}({t}^{2}-1)\cdot 1+{t}^{2}({t}^{2}-1+1)\cdot 2t\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}5{t}^{4}-5{t}^{2}+2{t}^{5}\,dt \\  & ={[{t}^{5}-\frac{5}{3}{t}^{3}+\frac{{t}^{6}}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =[{2}^{5}-\frac{5}{3}(2)^{3}+\frac{{2}^{6}}{3}]-[0] \\  & =32-\frac{40}{3}+\frac{64}{3} \\  & =40\end{aligned}
$$
